title: AXI4 Alignment and Byte-Lane Selection
description: Compare an aligned transfer with an unaligned INCR start on a 64-bit data bus; inspect each snapshot to connect AxSIZE, the byte address, and the WSTRB lanes that may carry valid bytes.

annotations.message: Aligned case: AWSIZE=2 permits up to four bytes and AWADDR 0x1000 is a four-byte boundary.
The aligned write uses byte lanes 0–3. WSTRB, not WDATA position alone, identifies the bytes that update.
Unaligned INCR case: the accepted start address is 0x1001. AXI permits this start; a WRAP start would have to be transfer-size aligned.
The first unaligned transfer uses lanes 1–3 of the aligned 0x1000 word. Address low bits and WSTRB must describe a consistent byte selection.
The next INCR transfer address is aligned to 0x1004 and uses lanes 4–7. The slave derives this beat address from the accepted burst controls.
